body:
Plan: EX-06 + EX-07.

Problem
Initial-radius foreground-first streaming exists, but there is no deterministic boundary-crossing benchmark. Remaining terrain/water/precombine setup and some mesh/upload/LOD operations are atomic, while LOD uses attempt counts rather than a measured wall-clock deadline.

Acceptance
- Deterministic camera/player path crosses at least two cell boundaries.
- Emit queue wait, worker parse, main-thread apply, unload, LOD, and whole-frame p50/p95/max timings per cell.
- Every NIF finalization, ordinary static placement, terrain/water/precombine phase, texture/mesh upload, BLAS build, and LOD provider yields under one shared measured deadline.
- Budget by elapsed time plus byte/mesh batches, not attempt count alone.
- Detect frame hitches above the agreed threshold and name the largest atomic unit.
- Run at minimum on FNV WastelandNV and one newer-engine worldspace (Skyrim Tamriel or FO4 Commonwealth).

comments.body:
2026-08-04 execution update (EX-06/EX-07):

- Added deterministic grid-cross traversal across three complete exterior cells.
- Added bounded queue, worker, apply, unload, LOD, supersession, pending-depth, and frame p50/p95/max telemetry; the smoke gate requires one full-detail and one LOD settlement per crossing.
- Live baseline: FNV full/LOD max 1.17/1.21 s; FO3 47.2/6.1 ms; Oblivion 0.91/1.50 s; Skyrim 8.10/8.14 s.
- FO4 exposed repeated 600+ MiB global-geometry rebuilds, then VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST. Rebuild batching plus a large-buffer idle safety path removed the device loss and reduced about 100 rebuilds to one per settled transaction.
- FO4 precombined application now yields between hashes. Worst apply slice fell from 2,546 ms to 293 ms.

The 900-frame FO4 gate remains red by design: first full/LOD settlement is 7.23/7.25 s, unload max is 745 ms, frame max is 816 ms, crossing two is superseded, and the final crossing remains unsettled. Next EX-07 slice is sub-hash CSG decode/upload/BLAS yielding, then resumable teardown.

Follow-up after validating pacing and rejecting a regressive sub-hash design:

- grid-cross now pauses its logical movement clock while the current full-detail + LOD boundary is active. Hold frames are still rendered and included in bench distributions, so renderer FPS no longer shortens the streaming window or makes the benchmark supersede itself.
- FO4 now passes all three independent crossings: full_samples=3, lod_samples=3, superseded=0, unsettled=0, with no Vulkan failure.
- Current FO4 tails are full 18.71 s, LOD 18.73 s, unload 848 ms, apply 315 ms, frame max 860 ms.
- A mesh-level precombine experiment reached apply max 145 ms but increased first settlement from 7.23 s to 32.73 s due many tiny BLAS submissions. That experiment was removed. The next implementation must defer/move single-hash work without fragmenting GPU submission throughput.

FO4 EX-06/07 update: landed once-per-boundary unload finalization (3205506d), bounded unload phase telemetry, and storage-oriented World::despawn_batch (ede92928). The instrumented baseline attributed 757.79 ms of an 836.69 ms unload to repeated per-entity despawn. Batch removal sorts/deduplicates victims once, acquires each storage once, keeps sparse removals O(1), and linearly compacts packed storage once. The same adaptive 900-logical-frame gate still passes 3/3 settled crossings with 100,633 entities / 24,959 draws and no device loss. unload max fell to 100.96 ms, dispatch to 101.64 ms, and despawn to 13.13 ms (58x lower); GPU release is now the unload tail at 83.20 ms. apply max remains 316.40 ms, frame max 547.95 ms, and full/LOD settlement 19.06/19.08 s, so EX-07 remains open on single-hash apply/BLAS/global-geometry throughput.

EX-07 follow-up measurement: per-hash instrumentation separates CSG/archive preparation, CPU spawn/upload, and the existing batched BLAS submission. Boundary cells show prepare <=21 ms and BLAS 20-24 ms, while CPU entity creation plus texture/mesh upload reaches 273-385 ms. A revised mesh cursor accumulated every BLAS spec and submitted exactly once per hash, but per-mesh CPU yielding still serialized too much work behind render cadence: crossing 1 settled in 50.27 s, crossing 2 in 105.66 s, and the 300 s hard timeout fired before crossing 3 settled. The cursor was removed. The retained code is diagnostic only; the next implementation must preserve CPU wall throughput, likely through worker-side preparation or calibrated upload batches, while retaining one BLAS batch per hash.

EX-07 teardown update: mesh and texture registry drops now batch holder-counted releases and purge dead cache mappings once, while retaining per-freed-handle descriptor fallback and deferred GPU destruction. FO4 live gate passes unchanged at 100,633 entities / 24,959 draws with 3/3 settlement and no device loss. unload_gpu_max fell 81.20 -> 23.16 ms, unload 98.88 -> 40.18 ms, and dispatch 99.77 -> 40.82 ms. Apply remains 291.23 ms and frame max 551.43 ms. Logs align the frame tail with the coherent 800-900 MiB global geometry rebuild and device-idle safety fallback, so capacity-managed global geometry is now the next renderer P0.

## Partial: the two pure-CPU gaps landed in e4ab12e8

#2376 stays open — the rest needs a GPU and on-disk game data.

### Already existed (worth recording before the new work)

**Acceptance item 1 is done and was done before this issue was filed.** `--bench-camera grid-cross` travels three complete cells east, which guarantees three boundary crossings from any starting X, with a 30% settle tail. Whole-frame p50/p95/max were also already emitted by `main`'s bench line, and the resumable cell apply already yielded against a `FrameTimeBudget` covering NIF finalization, terrain/water/precombine setup and ordinary static placement.

### Landed

**Deadline-bounded LOD (EX-07).** The three distant-LOD providers were bounded only by an attempt count — two per provider on an idle frame, **no time bound at all**. Attempts are wildly non-uniform: one is an archive extract + NIF parse + import + GPU upload of a macro-mesh whose footprint depends on its LOD band, and since #2371 the coarse bands stream quads covering up to 32×32 cells. Two of those can overrun a frame as easily as twenty cheap ones, and no attempt count can tell them apart.

`LodWorkBudget` now carries a deadline alongside its attempt cap, and `step_streaming` computes **one instant that bounds the whole streaming step** — apply and LOD both — rather than each stage starting a fresh allowance wherever the previous finished. The attempt cap is kept rather than replaced: it is what stops a large terrain ring starving the active object scheme, which a shared deadline alone would not do. Both budgets stay cooperative (one unit always admitted), so a frame whose apply consumed the allowance cannot stall the ring forever. The deterministic full-radius bootstrap stays untimed.

**Per-phase distributions (EX-06).** Every phase reported average + max. `StreamingLatencySummary` now keeps a 128-sample ring behind its all-time count/total/max, so percentiles are *exact* over the window while the aggregate stays constant-memory — a bucketed histogram of the same size would only approximate. `max` deliberately stays all-time: a hitch that scrolled out of the window still happened. `bench_line` emits a p50/p95/p100 triple for **queue wait, worker parse, apply, unload, LOD slice, and full detail**, using the same nearest-rank convention as `bench_frame_distribution` so per-phase and whole-frame numbers in one line are read identically.

### Explicitly *not* covered — I checked rather than assumed

Item 3 says *every* phase yields under the shared deadline. After walking every `should_yield()` call site:

- **BLAS builds are outside the streaming budget entirely** — `build_global_blas_for_draws` is called from the render path (`main.rs`), not the apply path. This is the largest remaining unbudgeted unit and the most likely hitch source.
- **Texture uploads** are batched at yield points (`flush_pending_cell_textures`) but the flush itself is not budgeted.
- **No byte/mesh batch axis** yet — item 4 asks for elapsed time *plus* byte/mesh batches; this delivers elapsed time plus attempt count.
- **No hitch detection** (item 5): nothing flags a frame above threshold or names the largest atomic unit. This needs per-unit attribution, not just per-phase slices, and is the natural next slice.
- **Item 6** (run on FNV WastelandNV + Skyrim Tamriel / FO4 Commonwealth) needs game data and a GPU.

### Verification

7 files, scoped to `byroredux` (3 of them are one-line call-site updates for the new parameter). 5 new regression tests: two pinning the LOD deadline behaviour (including that an already-elapsed deadline still admits exactly one attempt), three pinning the percentile maths, the all-time-max-survives-wrap invariant, and the bench-line fields. Clippy clean; full workspace suite run once (79 targets green). The one failure, `render::fire_lights::derived_reach_is_currently_oversized`, is pre-existing and unrelated — it fails identically on a clean tree.

Note on scope: this touched 7 files rather than the 5 the fix-issue flow suggests pausing at. I stopped here rather than also taking hitch detection, which would have genuinely ballooned it.

Broken down per `docs/engine/exterior-readiness-plan.md`'s 2026-08-23 investigation, which found most of the originally-suspected EX-06/07 bottlenecks (aggregate apply pacing, LOD budgeting) already fixed. The one remaining genuinely-open piece is filed as #3298 (make `MeshRegistry::rebuild_geometry_ssbo` yield mid-rebuild instead of one atomic Vulkan call).
